Question:
Are there any processes in place to assess if public sector bodies are charging for data above marginal cost? (please see directive (EU) 2019/1024 on open data and the reuse of public sector information).

For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify the process(es).
Explanation from 2023:
In accordance with the current legal framework in Bulgaria and through the Law on Access to Public Information, information from the public sector is provided for reuse free of charge or after payment of a fee, which cannot exceed the material costs of reproducing and providing the information. There are certain exceptions to this principle.
The processes used to identify Public Sector Organizations that charge data fees beyond marginal costs are a result of data requests received from interested parties.
The data department team analyzes the processes of pricing and payment of the data above the marginal costs, identifies the high value data according to the competence of the relevant administration, which should be published in an open machine-readable format on the Portal. A connection is established between the data holders, the interested parties requesting the data and the data department as a mediator, and meetings are organized to establish the details of the method of providing the data and the legal grounds for their provision at the present time.
Once meetings are organized between the relevant departments or working groups are formed, the purpose of which is to review the legal basis for the creation, maintenance and dissemination of the relevant data sets. The relevant regulations and documents defining the tariffs and fees are reviewed and, after assessing their importance and significance for users, a decision is made to provide the data with free access or up to marginal costs.
As a result, they are included in the annual list of data sets by priority areas, approved by a Ministerial Council Decision. The responsible administrations, for their part, should change their legal grounds for collecting fees for those included in the list of data approved by the decision of the Council of Ministers.

ElasticSearch is a full-text search and data analysis system. It offers possibilities for storing and processing large volumes of information. The system supports the construction of clusters of single installations, which increase productivity and guarantee the impossibility of work.

Centralized storage of data collected from log files. It allows automated processing of the collected data, as well as preparation of various statistical reports and visualizations. In addition, the system allows for automated output when events are initiated.
License: open source software, distributed under the GNU GPL.

3.6.9. Data migration tool

3.6.10. Automated data entry tool
The automated data entry tool is designed as a set of components located in the so-called "container" which is a system running on different operating systems. The installation of the automated data entry tool requires the installation of a special pad that implements the support of this container. For the base of work, choose Docker Community Edition. Question:

Explanation from 2023:
Open data is the public information collected, created and maintained by public sector organizations and published in an open machine-readable format (CSV, RDF, XML, JSON, etc.), allowing re-use for commercial or non-commercial purposes.
Reuse of public sector information is the use also for commercial or non-commercial purposes other than the original purpose for which it was created within the powers or functions of a public sector organization. The provision of public sector information to a public sector organization in connection with the exercise of its powers or functions is not reuse within the meaning of Access to Public Information Act. (Article 2a, APIA).

The development and implementation of a virtual online learning platform will provide flexible and affordable forms of learning such as online distance learning courses and electronic resources for self-study.
After the creation and implementation of the virtual e-learning platform under Component 1, all courses in an electronic environment for the training of unemployed and employed persons, organized within the framework of the active labor market policy and financed from the state budget and from the ESF+ under the "Development of human resources", will be held through it.
The virtual e-learning platform will be linked to the My Competence Competence Assessment Information System, which presents competency models describing the skills and competencies required to successfully perform key positions and tools, as well as databases and electronic registers relevant to the training of adults - the National Labor Market Database of the Employment Agency (EA), the Electronic Register of Vocational Training Centers of the National Agency for Vocational Education and Training (NAPEO), etc.
The Platform will also have access to the training providers, as well as control bodies (e.g. MTSP, AZ, NAPOO, employers, etc.). They will be able to monitor and control the implementation of the trainings in real time. At any moment during the training period, it will be possible to check the attendance of the trainees, the completion of the curriculum by days, the success rate through access to the exam materials and tests, access to the materials and questionnaires for the evaluation of the training, etc. In this way, compliance with the regulatory requirements for the organization of training and the quality of the conducted training will be monitored.
Total estimated financial resource - BGN 379,470,088.
Project implementation period – 54 months (2022-2026)
Expected results:
The digital learning platform to be fully functional;
To operate 760 digital clubs in which access to the training platform will be provided
Approximately 500,000 unemployed and employed persons have received basic and/or intermediate level digital skills training
Approximately 100,000 unemployed and employed persons have validated their basic and/or intermediate level knowledge of digital skills
